groups.name: Rain
groups.note: Rain-led recordings from xeno-canto, in the direction of Rain on Leaves.

groups.name: Water
groups.note: Streams, a torrent and a calm sea: steady beds of moving water, new to the app.

groups.name: Frogs
groups.note: Dense, even choruses like Frog Pond, two of them from the south of France.

groups.name: Night
groups.note: A single steady night voice, like the scops owl.

items.name: Carpathian Rain
items.why: Last round's runner-up to Rain on Leaves: heavier, very steady rain in an old beech forest at dawn, the most rain-led of the long recordings. You haven't heard it yet.
items.listen: water hitting the microphones, and a song thrush repeating a phrase.

items.name: Pyrenean Drizzle
items.why: Light rain on a spring afternoon in a Pyrenean reserve, with blue tits, firecrests and a wood pigeon softly underneath. Gentler and brighter than Rain on Leaves.
items.listen: how much is rain and how much is birds.

items.name: Thunder in the Beeches
items.place: Beech wood near Fischach, Swabia, Bavaria, Germany
items.why: An early-summer evening storm: rain falling through a beech wood with thunder rolling around it. The only storm in the list; its energy sits low and warm (150–800 Hz).
items.listen: the thunder. It makes the level swing more than anything else here (LRA 12 LU), which can wake you.

items.name: Mountain Stream
items.why: A winter dawn in the Pyrenees with the low roar of a stream downhill and a few tits and thrushes. The steadiest recording found in this round (level SD 0.6 dB), like a soft brown noise.
items.listen: rumble. A quarter of the energy is below 150 Hz, and the source is quiet (−40 LUFS), so the preview lifts it 16 dB.

items.name: Creek and Tawny Owl
items.why: Dusk in an Austrian valley: a creek running to one side, the last song thrushes, blackbirds and robins, and a tawny owl. The owl-and-water night that the notes call “still open”.
items.listen: the birds at the start. Dusk choruses fade, so the loop would hold them all night.

items.name: Pine Forest Torrent
items.place: Sierra de Francia y Quilamas, Salamanca, Spain
items.why: A Scots pine forest in June with a torrent and waterfall further off: a bright, hissy water bed (mostly 3–8 kHz) with chaffinches and a blackcap over it.
items.listen: whether the water hiss reads as calm or harsh.

items.name: Calm Arctic Sea
items.why: A calm September morning a few metres from the shore, with small waves lapping and two black guillemot calls far out. The only sea in the list. Uncompressed source.
items.listen: the guillemots, and the length: the recording (8:59) is only just long enough for one loop.

items.name: Stream at Sunset
items.place: Small valley by a chapel, Cordes-sur-Ciel, Tarn, France
items.why: A quiet valley at sunset with a small stream, a firecrest, a song thrush and a roe deer. Very French and very still.
items.listen: hiss first. The source is very quiet (−47 LUFS), so the preview lifts it 27 dB. This is the trap that sank the Somme marsh last round.

items.name: Tree Frog Pond
items.why: A March evening pond near Toulouse full of Mediterranean tree frogs, with coots and a heron. The steadiest chorus found (level SD 0.6 dB, loudest 1 % only 2.4 dB over the bed) and loud, so nothing is lifted.
items.listen: whether one pitch for seven minutes is lulling or wearing.

items.name: Marsh Frogs in the Tarn
items.why: A March night at a pond in the Tarn: marsh frogs and Mediterranean tree frogs together, with more movement than the Lavalette pond but still even.
items.listen: the marsh frogs' laugh-like calls, which are livelier than the rest.

items.name: Tree Frogs and Reed Crickets
items.place: El Condado salt marsh, near Sevilla, Spain
items.why: Last round's favourite runner-up: a clean, steady wall of Mediterranean tree frogs over reed crickets in a tamarisk-lined marsh. It passed every check when it was built.
items.listen: how close it sounds to Frog Pond, which is from the same marshes.

items.name: Nightjar at Midnight
items.why: A European nightjar churring through a May night in the Aude, with a woodlark and a distant tawny owl. Almost all of it is one soft 2 kHz drone, as steady as anything here.
items.listen: whether the churr is hypnotic or tiring. That was the doubt last round.

note: Round 2 verdicts, by ear. Keeps were built into the app (builtAs = their id in soundscapes.config.json). The five A2O candidates were also passed and are only listed in docs/curation.md, since A2O is no longer used.
